all_candidates.text: Certain medical conditions affecting the eyes, such as allergies, infections (conjunctivitis), or dry eye syndrome (leading to compensatory tearing), can cause excessive tear production.
Tears can be caused by a strong emotional response like sadness, happiness, or anger, which triggers the lacrimal glands to produce more tears.
Physical pain or injury to the eye or surrounding area can lead to reflex tearing as a protective mechanism.
Involuntary muscle spasms or neurological signals can also trigger tear production even without apparent external stimuli or emotional states.
Irritation from foreign objects in the eye (dust, smoke, an eyelash) or environmental factors (wind, cold air) stimulates the lacrimal glands to wash away the irritant.
